zh.summary: 分清弱點成因、評估對象與方法，組合五個評估維度，判斷掃描證據與修正優先順序。

sourceBody.text: 這一課最重要的觀念是：
「系統哪裡有問題」、「要從哪裡檢查」與「有沒有證據證明問題存在」，是三件不同的事。
你可以把弱點評估想成醫生替病人健康檢查。
醫生不能只看病人有沒有發燒，就宣布他完全健康。同樣地，資安工程師也不能只跑一次弱點掃描，就宣布系統沒有安全問題。
一、先理解：什麼是弱點（Vulnerability）？
假設你經營一間銀行。
銀行裡有金庫、監視器、保全、門禁系統及員工。
某天發現銀行有安全問題，可能是以下五種原因：

visual.caption: 圖 1｜五種弱點成因
visual.description: 依成因安排修正；五種分類可能重疊，編號只供對照。

items.title: 1. 設計缺陷（Design Flaw）
items.body:
銀行最初設計時，就沒有規定誰能進入金庫。

問題出在「制度或系統規則一開始就沒設計好」。

items.title: 2. 實作缺陷（Implementation Flaw）
items.body:
銀行規定只有經理能進入金庫，但工程師寫門禁程式時，忘記檢查身分。

問題出在「規則正確，程式卻寫錯」。

items.title: 3. 設定錯誤（Misconfiguration）
items.body:
門禁系統本來有身分驗證功能，但管理員把它設成所有人都能進入。

問題出在「功能正常，設定卻不安全」。

items.title: 4. 尚未修補的已知缺陷（Unpatched Vulnerability）
items.body:
門禁廠商發現某個版本有安全漏洞，已經發布更新，但銀行還沒安裝。

問題出在「已經有修補方法，卻還沒完成修補」。

items.title: 5. 管理與流程缺口（Process Weakness）
items.body:
某位經理已經離職，但銀行沒有註銷他的門禁權限。

問題出在「人員管理或維護流程不完善」。

sourceBody.text: 這五種問題都可能讓未經授權的人進入金庫，但是修正的方法完全不同。
這就是為什麼要做「弱點分類」。
弱點分類的目的，不是背五個英文名詞，而是找到真正原因，決定應該由誰修正。 而且分類可能重疊，例如軟體沒更新，也可能同時代表維護流程失效。
二、弱點評估類型：我們究竟要檢查什麼？
接著把銀行換成一套公司的資訊系統。
這個系統可能同時具有伺服器、網路、網站、資料庫、Wi-Fi 與雲端儲存。
不同位置要採取不同的檢查方式。

visual.caption: 圖 2｜同一套系統的多個評估層級
visual.description: 上層是網路觀察視角；下方四類互補。連線只表示同一系統中的關聯，不代表資料流或檢查先後。

items.title: 使用者與網路
items.body: Network assessment：觀察網路出入口與可接觸的服務。

items.title: 網站 / API
items.body: Application：檢查登入、身分驗證、授權與程式邏輯。

items.title: 伺服器
items.body: Host-based：檢查作業系統、更新、權限與設定。

items.title: 資料庫
items.body: Database：檢查帳號、資料存取權限與安全設定。

items.title: 雲端 / Wi-Fi
items.body: Cloud / Wireless：檢查雲端資源權限、Wi-Fi 保護與網路隔離。

sourceBody.text: 概念示意：同一套系統可以從多個層級進行安全評估，這些檢查彼此互補。

rows: 作業系統、更新、權限、設定
開放的連接埠、服務、暴露範圍
登入、身分驗證、授權、程式邏輯
帳號、資料存取權限、安全設定
雲端資源權限、Wi-Fi 保護、網路隔離

sourceBody.text: 例如：
你掃描一台 Web Server，發現作業系統已經更新到最新版本。
這能代表網站一定安全嗎？
不能。
因為作業系統的漏洞與網站程式的漏洞，是不同的事情。
即使伺服器完全更新，網站工程師仍可能把授權邏輯寫錯，讓 A 使用者看見 B 使用者的資料。
所以，Host-based Assessment 沒發現問題，不代表 Application Assessment 也不會發現問題。
三、External 與 Internal：站在哪裡檢查？
想像你要檢查一棟公司的辦公大樓。
External Assessment
外部評估
站在大樓外面，檢查大門、外牆、外部能接觸的設備。
Internal Assessment
內部評估
在取得授權後進入大樓，檢查內部門禁、區域隔離與權限。
換成資安情境：
外部評估可能是在授權條件下，從 Internet 觀察公司的網站、VPN 或其他對外服務。
內部評估則可能從公司內部的指定網段，檢查內部伺服器與服務的存取限制。
重要的推理是：
外部看不到某台資料庫，只能代表「這次外部檢查沒觀察到它」，不能代表資料庫不存在，更不能證明它安全。
另外，Internal / External 說的是測試位置，並不是檢查者是不是公司員工。
四、Active 與 Passive：怎麼檢查？
這裡最容易混淆。
假設你想知道一間房子有沒有人在裡面。

visual.caption: 圖 3｜主動與被動：取得證據的方式
visual.description: 兩種觀察方式並列互補，都需要授權。

items.title: Active 主動式
items.body: 你主動敲門、按門鈴，看看是否有人回應。

items.title: Passive 被動式
items.body: 你觀察現有的監視畫面或進出紀錄，不主動敲門。

sourceBody.text: 在資訊系統中：

items: Active Scanning：工具主動向目標發送測試請求，根據回應判斷服務、版本或可能的弱點。
Passive Assessment：分析既有網路封包、日誌或其他觀察資料，不透過主動探測取得回應。

sourceBody.text: 兩者各有侷限。
主動式可能獲得更多直接證據，但也可能增加系統負載，甚至影響老舊服務。
被動式通常不會因為探測請求增加目標負載，但如果相關事件沒有發生、沒有被記錄，或不在觀察範圍內，就可能完全看不到。
而且被動觀察也可能涉及敏感資料，並不是不需要授權。
五、還有兩組很重要的分類
Authenticated / Unauthenticated（是否使用帳號驗證）
假設你檢查一間飯店。
Unauthenticated 就像沒有房卡的訪客，只能看到公開大廳。
Authenticated 則像持有獲准房卡的人，可以檢查授權範圍內的房間與設施。
在資安評估中，具身分驗證的掃描通常能取得更多系統內部資訊，例如已安裝套件與設定。但具備帳號，不代表擁有所有存取權限。
Automated / Manual（由工具還是人來檢查）
Automated 像自動體檢機器，適合大量、重複且可規則化的檢查。
Manual 像醫生親自問診，適合需要理解情境、業務邏輯及判斷例外的問題。
實務上通常兩者搭配。
六、所有分類其實是不同的維度
這是一個很重要的整合觀念。
假設主管要求你檢查公司內部的 Linux 伺服器，並提供獲准的掃描帳號。
你可能同時選擇：

visual.caption: 圖 4｜同一場弱點評估的五個維度
visual.description: 五項同時成立；編號供閱讀，不代表執行步驟或實測通過。

items.title: 1. 檢查對象：Host-based
items.body: Linux 伺服器

items.title: 2. 檢查位置：Internal
items.body: 從內部網路檢查

items.title: 3. 取得證據：Active
items.body: 主動發送探測與檢查請求

items.title: 4. 驗證身分：Authenticated
items.body: 使用核准的掃描帳號

items.title: 5. 執行方式：Automated
items.body: 先以工具執行重複檢查

sourceBody.text: 這五種標籤完全不衝突，因為每一種都在回答不同問題。
也就是說，評估類型不是單選題，而是可以組合的檢查策略。
七、實際案例：掃描器說有問題，代表一定能入侵嗎？
假設某套公司訂單系統出現以下結果。

rows: 實際版本、修補狀態、是否符合漏洞成立條件
某項設定可能不符合政策
哪些資料可讀、預期權限、實際影響
C：A 帳號讀到 B 的訂單
有跨帳號存取的具體現象
是否違反原定授權規則、影響範圍

sourceBody.text: 我們可以把弱點評估理解為逐步累積證據的過程：

visual.caption: 圖 5｜逐步累積弱點證據
visual.description: 箭頭表示工作順序；受控驗證須必要且在授權範圍內。

items.title: 發現線索
items.body: 工具回報套件可能有漏洞

items.title: 核對成立條件
items.body: 確認版本、設定、影響條件及政策

items.title: 授權範圍內驗證
items.body: 必要時進行受控測試並記錄結果

items.title: 評估影響、修正與複驗
items.body: 確認缺陷是否修正，正常功能是否保留

sourceBody.text: 要特別分清楚：

items: 發現可能的弱點，不等於證明弱點可被利用。
證明存在可利用的弱點，不等於證明系統已經遭人入侵。
修正一個弱點，也不等於整套系統已經安全。

sourceBody.text: 另外，Severity（嚴重程度）不等於 Priority（處理優先順序）。前者關注可能造成多大傷害；後者還要衡量暴露情況、資產重要性、現有防護和修正急迫性。
例如，一個能直接讓外部訪客讀取敏感資料的設定錯誤，可能比只在特定內部條件下才會觸發的高分漏洞，更需要優先處理。
八、最後用一句話串起 M05-01、M05-02、M05-03

rows: M05-01 弱點評估與滲透測試
我們要找出問題，還是進一步證明實際影響？
M05-02 資產盤點與評估範圍
有哪些資產？這次獲准檢查哪些？
M05-03 弱點分類與評估類型
問題可能出在哪裡？應該用什麼角度檢查？

sourceBody.text: 因此，一次專業的弱點評估，不是「開啟掃描器、按下開始、拿到報告」就結束。
而是先確定資產與授權範圍，再選擇適合的評估方式，辨認問題成因、核對證據，最後提出修正與驗證方法。
九、理解檢核：用一個案例測試是否真正學會
1. 某公司網站的作業系統完全更新，但使用者 A 可以讀取使用者 B 的私人訂單。這比較可能是哪一種弱點？
A. 設定錯誤
B. 設計或實作上的授權缺陷
C. 未修補的作業系統漏洞
2. 你使用經過授權的帳號，從內部網路透過工具主動檢查 Linux 主機。這同時符合哪些分類？
A. External、Passive、Unauthenticated
B. Internal、Active、Authenticated、Automated
C. Internal、Passive、Unauthenticated
3. 掃描器沒有找到已知版本漏洞，是否可以宣布系統安全？
A. 可以，代表沒有弱點
B. 不行，因為設定、權限與應用程式邏輯仍可能有問題
C. 可以，只要掃描器是最新版本

paragraphs: 問題一答案 B。作業系統已更新不會自動修正網站授權邏輯。A 的設定錯誤在其他情境也可能造成越權，但題目線索最支持設計或實作上的授權缺陷；C 沒有未修補作業系統漏洞的證據。仍須核對原定權限及實際程式，才能判定根因。
問題二答案 B。內部網路對應 Internal，主動發送檢查請求對應 Active，核准帳號對應 Authenticated，工具執行重複檢查對應 Automated。A 的三個標籤都與情境不符；C 雖然位置正確，卻把主動且使用帳號的檢查誤寫成被動、未驗證。檢查對象也屬 Host-based。
問題三答案 B。這次掃描沒有回報已知版本漏洞，只能支持該工具、範圍及時間下的觀察；設定、權限及業務邏輯仍可能有問題。A 把沒有找到當成不存在，C 把工具更新當成完整安全保證。下一步依資產與授權範圍補足其他檢查。

sourceBody.text: 這三題涵蓋本課最核心的能力：辨識弱點原因、組合評估方式，以及判斷安全證據的限制。
十、來源與適用範圍
[NIST SP 800-115](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/115/final) 說明評估規劃、主動探測、被動觀察及各種技術的限制；本課五類成因是幫助找出修正責任的教學整理，並非互斥或完整的標準分類。銀行、飯店與訂單系統都是合成情境，沒有對真實系統執行掃描。
[FIRST CVSS v4.0 使用指南](https://www.first.org/cvss/user-guide) 說明嚴重程度評分需要搭配威脅、環境與組織情境判斷。本課不把嚴重程度直接當成處理優先順序。三題可先自行作答，再展開參考解析；頁面不送出、保存或批改個人答案。

en.summary: Separate vulnerability causes, assessment targets and methods; combine five dimensions and judge scanning evidence and remediation priority.

sourceBody.text: The central idea of this lesson is that “where a system has a problem,” “where and how to examine it,” and “whether evidence confirms the problem” are three different questions.

Think of vulnerability assessment as a medical checkup. A doctor cannot look only for fever and declare a patient completely healthy. Similarly, a security engineer cannot run one vulnerability scan and declare a system free of security problems.
1. What is a vulnerability?
Imagine that you operate a bank with a vault, cameras, guards, access-control equipment and employees. A security problem might arise from five different causes.

visual.caption: Figure 1 | Five causes of vulnerabilities
visual.description: Use causes to assign remediation. Categories can overlap; numbers identify entries, not a sequence.

items.title: 1. Design Flaw
items.body:
The bank never specified who may enter the vault.

The institution or system rules were incomplete from the start.

items.title: 2. Implementation Flaw
items.body:
The rule permits only the manager, but the engineer forgot to check identity in the access-control code.

The rule is correct; the program implements it incorrectly.

items.title: 3. Misconfiguration
items.body:
The access-control system supports authentication, but an administrator allows everyone to enter.

The feature works; its configuration is unsafe.

items.title: 4. Unpatched Vulnerability
items.body:
The vendor has released an update for a known flaw in the access-control version, but the bank has not installed it.

A fix exists, but patching is incomplete.

items.title: 5. Process Weakness
items.body:
A manager has left the bank, but the bank has not revoked the manager’s access.

Personnel management or maintenance procedures are incomplete.

sourceBody.text: All five problems could allow an unauthorized person into the vault, but they need different fixes. This is why we classify vulnerabilities.

The purpose is to identify the actual cause and decide who should correct it, rather than memorize five English terms. Categories can overlap: missing software updates may also indicate a failed maintenance process.
2. Assessment types: what are we examining?

Now replace the bank with a company information system. It may contain servers, networks, websites, databases, Wi-Fi and cloud storage at the same time. Different parts need different examination methods.

visual.caption: Figure 2 | Multiple assessment layers of one system
visual.description: The top is the network observation perspective; the four categories below complement it. Lines mean association within one system, not traffic or assessment order.

items.title: Users and network
items.body: Network assessment: examine network entry points and reachable services.

items.title: Website / API
items.body: Application: examine login, authentication, authorization and program logic.

items.title: Server
items.body: Host-based: examine the operating system, updates, permissions and configuration.

items.title: Database
items.body: Database: examine accounts, data-access permissions and security configuration.

items.title: Cloud / Wi-Fi
items.body: Cloud / Wireless: examine cloud-resource permissions, Wi-Fi protection and network isolation.

sourceBody.text: Conceptual illustration: one system can be assessed at multiple levels; these examinations complement one another.

rows: Cloud-resource permissions, Wi-Fi protection, network isolation

sourceBody.text: For example, you scan a Web Server and find that its operating system has all current updates. Does that prove the website is secure? No: operating-system flaws and website-programming flaws are different things.

Even on a fully updated server, a developer could implement authorization incorrectly and allow user A to see user B’s data. No findings in a Host-based Assessment do not imply that an Application Assessment would also find nothing.
3. External and Internal: where do you examine from?
Imagine inspecting a company office building.
External Assessment means examining the main entrance, exterior walls and externally reachable equipment while standing outside the building.
Internal Assessment means entering with authorization to examine internal access controls, separation between areas and permissions.

In security work, an external assessment may observe the company website, VPN or other Internet-facing services under authorized conditions. An internal assessment may start in a specified company network segment to examine access restrictions on internal servers and services.

The key inference is that failing to observe a database from outside means only that this external examination did not observe it. It does not show that the database does not exist or that it is secure.
Internal / External describes the testing position, rather than whether the examiner is a company employee.
4. Active and Passive: how do you examine?
This distinction is easy to confuse. Imagine trying to find out whether someone is inside a house.

visual.caption: Figure 3 | Active and passive ways to gather evidence
visual.description: The two complementary approaches are parallel; both require authorization.

items.title: Active
items.body: You knock or ring the bell to see whether someone responds.

items.title: Passive
items.body: You examine existing surveillance footage or entry records without knocking.

sourceBody.text: In information systems:

items: Active Scanning: a tool sends test requests to a target and uses responses to infer services, versions or possible vulnerabilities.
Passive Assessment: examine existing network packets, logs or other observation data without obtaining responses through active probing.

sourceBody.text: Both have limits. Active methods may obtain more direct evidence, but may also add load or disrupt older services.

Passive methods usually add no probing-request load to the target. However, if relevant events never occur, are not recorded or fall outside the observation scope, the problem may remain completely invisible.
Passive observation can also involve sensitive data and still requires authorization.
5. Two other important classification pairs
Authenticated / Unauthenticated: do you use an account?

Imagine inspecting a hotel. Unauthenticated is like a visitor without a room card, limited to the public lobby. Authenticated is like someone holding an approved card who can examine rooms and facilities within the permitted scope.
Authenticated scanning often provides more internal system information, such as installed packages and configuration. Having an account does not grant every permission.
Automated / Manual: does a tool or a person examine it?
Automated methods resemble an automatic checkup machine: they suit large numbers of repetitive checks that can be expressed as rules.
Manual methods resemble a doctor’s consultation: they suit questions that require context, business logic and judgment about exceptions. In practice the two are usually combined.
6. These classifications describe different dimensions
This is an important integrating idea. Suppose a manager asks you to examine an internal Linux server and provides an approved scanning account. You might choose all of these labels together:

visual.caption: Figure 4 | Five dimensions of one assessment
visual.description: All five labels can apply together. Numbers guide reading; they are neither execution steps nor passed checks.

items.title: 1. Target: Host-based
items.body: A Linux server

items.title: 2. Position: Internal
items.body: Examine it from the internal network

items.title: 3. Evidence collection: Active
items.body: Send probes and inspection requests

items.title: 4. Identity: Authenticated
items.body: Use an approved scanning account

items.title: 5. Execution: Automated
items.body: Begin with tools for repetitive checks

sourceBody.text: The five labels do not conflict because each answers a different question. Assessment types form a combinable examination strategy rather than a single-choice classification.
7. Does a scanner finding prove you can break in?
Suppose a company order system produces these findings.

rows: Actual version, patch status, required vulnerability conditions
B: A folder permits anonymous reads
Readable data, expected permissions, actual impact
C: Account A reads B’s order
Whether it violates the intended authorization rules, affected scope

sourceBody.text: Vulnerability assessment can be understood as accumulating evidence step by step:

visual.caption: Figure 5 | Accumulate vulnerability evidence step by step
visual.description: Arrows indicate work order. Controlled validation must be necessary and authorized.

items.title: Find a clue
items.body: A tool reports a potentially vulnerable package

items.title: Check the required conditions
items.body: Confirm version, configuration, impact conditions and policy

items.title: Validate within authorization
items.body: Perform a controlled test if necessary and record results

items.title: Assess impact, fix and retest
items.body: Confirm that the defect is fixed and normal functionality remains

sourceBody.text: Keep these conclusions separate:

items: Finding a possible vulnerability does not prove that it can be exploited.
Proving an exploitable vulnerability exists does not prove that someone has already broken into the system.
Fixing one vulnerability does not establish that the entire system is secure.

sourceBody.text: Severity is different from Priority. Severity concerns the potential harm; handling priority also considers exposure, asset importance, existing controls and remediation urgency.

For example, a misconfiguration that directly lets external visitors read sensitive data may need attention sooner than a highly scored vulnerability that triggers only under particular internal conditions.
8. Connect M05-01, M05-02 and M05-03

rows: M05-01 Vulnerability assessment and penetration testing
Are we finding problems or going further to demonstrate actual impact?
M05-02 Asset inventory and assessment scope
Which assets exist, and which are authorized for this examination?
M05-03 Vulnerability classification and assessment types
Where might the problem originate, and which examination perspectives should we use?

sourceBody.text: A professional vulnerability assessment takes more than opening a scanner, pressing Start and obtaining a report.
First establish assets and authorized scope. Then choose suitable assessment methods, identify causes, check evidence and propose remediation and verification methods.
9. Check your understanding with a scenario
1. A company website’s operating system is fully updated, but user A can read user B’s private orders. Which cause is most likely?
A. Misconfiguration
B. A design or implementation authorization flaw
C. An unpatched operating-system vulnerability
2. You use an authorized account and a tool to actively examine a Linux host from the internal network. Which classifications apply together?
A. External, Passive, Unauthenticated
B. Internal, Active, Authenticated, Automated
C. Internal, Passive, Unauthenticated
3. A scanner finds no known version vulnerabilities. Can you declare the system secure?
A. Yes; it means there are no vulnerabilities
B. No; configuration, permissions and application logic may still have problems
C. Yes, provided the scanner is up to date

paragraphs: Question 1: B. Operating-system updates do not automatically fix application authorization. Misconfiguration (A) can cause unauthorized access in other circumstances, but the stated clues best support a design or implementation authorization flaw. C has no evidence of an unpatched operating-system flaw. Check intended permissions and the actual program to determine the root cause.

Question 2: B. The internal network means Internal; sending inspection requests means Active; an approved account means Authenticated; tool-based repetitive checks mean Automated. All three labels in A contradict the scenario. C gets the position right but incorrectly calls the active, authenticated examination passive and unauthenticated. The target is also Host-based.

Question 3: B. No reported known version flaws supports only an observation for this tool, scope and time. Configuration, permissions and business logic may still be flawed. A confuses no finding with no flaw; C mistakes updated tools for a complete security guarantee. Next, fill examination gaps within the asset and authorization scope.

sourceBody.text: These three questions cover the core skills: identifying vulnerability causes, combining assessment methods and judging the limits of security evidence.
10. Sources and scope

[NIST SP 800-115](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/115/final) explains assessment planning, active probing, passive observation and the limits of different techniques. This lesson’s five causes are a teaching framework for assigning remediation, not an exhaustive or mutually exclusive standard taxonomy. The bank, hotel and order system are synthetic examples; no real systems were scanned.

The [FIRST CVSS v4.0 User Guide](https://www.first.org/cvss/user-guide) explains that severity scoring needs threat, environmental and organizational context. This lesson does not equate severity with handling priority. Answer the three questions yourself before opening the reference explanations; the page does not submit, store or grade personal answers.
